source.title: A Low-Rank Subspace Analysis of LLM Interventions
source.authors: Angira Sharma; C. D. de Witt; P. Torr; A. Calinescu; Jia-Lin Yu

record.tranche_reason: The paper refines the one-direction account by testing rank-1 versus low-rank behavior subspaces in LLMs. Its results argue that rank 1 is insufficient for the behavior representations studied, rather than testing toy-model feature superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper cites and discusses superposition, but its experiments concern behavior-category subspaces and projection interventions, not sparse features, feature co-activation, neurons, or SAE dictionaries. The rank ablation in Appendix D is the direct result bearing on V6; other intervention and overlap results do not directly measure the dimensionality claim.
record.test_reason: The study cites Elhage et al. (2022) only as background on overlapping representations. Its experiments use PCA subspaces of contrastive behaviour activations (refusal, sycophancy categories) in instruct LLMs and study cross-behaviour effects of projection interventions. It never measures sparse features, neurons, SAE dictionaries or toy models. The Appendix D rank ablation tunes the rank of the study's own intervention subspace (r=1,2,3). Projecting out more dimensions naturally removes more variance, so the ablation is a method hyperparameter choice, not a test of whether superposed features are 1-D. It is a related but different construct: behaviour-level subspaces, not features in superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misweighted. The main conclusion is about intervention side effects, not dimensionality. Interventions on one behaviour change others asymmetrically. Subspace overlap shows where cross-effects can occur, and decision coupling governs their size and direction. The rank-1-vs-rank-2 finding is a secondary appendix result justifying their rank choice (r=2 as a practical tradeoff).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses PCA-derived behavior subspaces and activation projection interventions in instruction-tuned LLMs, rather than toy networks and sparse-feature superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The rank ablation reports different intervention effects across ranks: rank 1 has weaker self-effects, while rank 3 increases collateral effects relative to rank 2.

fits_no_version.finding: After decision residualization, behaviour-category contrast representations lack a well-separated leading eigenvalue (Appendix K). Rank-1 projection gives weaker self-effects than rank 2 (mean |ΔM| 2.1 vs 4.3, Gemma-2-9B layer -8). Rank 3 raises collateral effects (5.1 vs 3.8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behaviour-level concepts (refusal categories) in instruct LLMs occupy low-rank multi-dimensional subspaces rather than single directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Behaviour subspaces overlap after residualization. Projecting out one category's subspace shifts other categories' decision margins, often comparably to self-effects. The effects are 147×–319× larger than with random rank-2 subspaces (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overlapping behaviour representations cause asymmetric cross-behaviour interference under linear interventions, modulated by alignment with the decision subspace.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
record.problems: The rank-ablation table is for one model and one layer; it reports no uncertainty for those values. The experiments concern behavior-category subspaces and do not establish feature-level superposition or the dimensionality of individual features.
record.rows_left_out: Other overlap and cross-category intervention results were not included because they test behavior transfer and decision coupling, not the dimensionality distinction in V6. No other reported rank-ablation values were left out.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity, transitions or geometry.
All: no neurons or capacity competition.
All: no neuron-level distribution or SAE features; only PCA of behaviour contrast vectors.
Whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. Only the rank of behaviour-category intervention subspaces is varied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'challenges' label is withdrawn. The rank ablation is a hyperparameter selection for the study's own projection method, in one model at one layer. It concerns PCA behaviour subspaces, not features in superposition. Authors caution against reading PCs as mechanisms.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular feature geometry are not tested.
The paper does not test neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared neuron dimensions.
The paper does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The paper does not measure features distributed across neurons or recover sparse features with an SAE.
The paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
It tests dimensionality of behavior-category subspaces via rank ablations, not whether individual features in superposition are inherently one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute self-intervention effect.
rows.note: The authors describe rank-1 self-effects as weak and the rank-1 representation as insufficient to capture category-specific structure.
rows.check: Rank-selection value for the study's own intervention subspace (Table 2). It measures intervention self-effect size, not the dimensionality of superposed features. Not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute self-intervention effect.
rows.note: The paper identifies rank 2 as a balanced rank choice; its self-effect is larger than at rank 1.
rows.check: Own-method rank hyperparameter value. A larger effect from projecting out more dimensions does not bear on V6.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute self-intervention effect.
rows.note: The paper says rank-3 self-effects are comparable to rank-2.
rows.check: Own-method rank hyperparameter value; not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute collateral intervention effect.
rows.note: This metric reports collateral effects, not dimensionality by itself.
rows.check: Collateral effect at rank 1 for own-method selection; not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute collateral intervention effect.
rows.note: This metric reports collateral effects, not dimensionality by itself.
rows.check: Collateral effect at rank 2 for own-method selection; not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Project out category subspaces and measure mean absolute collateral intervention effect.
rows.note: The paper says collateral effects increase substantially at rank 3; this metric alone does not establish feature dimensionality.
rows.check: Collateral effect at rank 3 for own-method selection; not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compare rank-1 category-subspace geometry with the overlap patterns from higher-rank subspaces.
rows.measure: Ability of rank-1 representations to recover category overlap patterns
rows.value: The paper states that rank-1 representations fail to recover the overlap patterns observed with low-rank subspaces.
rows.note: The rank-ablation discussion also says rank-1 category subspaces exhibit high geometric overlap, reflecting insufficient capacity to separate category-specific variation.
rows.check: 'Reversed' is unjustified. Rank-1 subspaces failing to reproduce rank-2 overlap patterns compares the study's own estimators. It says nothing about whether superposed features are 1-D. No numbers are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Rank ablation of behavior-category subspaces in Gemma-2-9B-IT at layer -8
reader_labels.reason: Rank 1 has weaker self-effects and fails to recover the higher-rank overlap patterns, while rank 2 produces larger self-effects; this challenges a one-direction account for these behavior representations (r1, r2, r7).
